full_text_checked: Read: full HTML article text (abstract, introduction, results Figs 2-11 descriptions, methods: preprocessing, EMD model, lobula unit dynamics, parameters, F-measure definition, discussion and limitations, data availability, acknowledgments, reference list). Code: GitHub repository listing and readme read; individual .m file contents (stimulus.m, LobulaUnits.m) were not opened, so code-level parameter values were not cross-checked against the text. Not accessed: supporting information files (videos, any S1 text), exact plotted values in figures (only text statements and figure captions were available, so many numbers exist only as curves).
task_and_output: Task: figure-ground discrimination (segmentation of a moving figure/bar from a textured background) from relative motion alone, plus reproduction of LC15-like (lobula columnar) response properties to bars vs moving gratings. Output: retinotopic maps of graded activity of model lobula units (Lr, Ll, Lm and intermediate Ir, Il, Im) at each time step; for evaluation these maps are thresholded at 50% of maximum (also 10/30/70/90% in Fig 4) into a binary foreground mask per frame. No centroid, bounding box, velocity estimate, presence score or identity output; no tracking over time beyond the instantaneous segmentation; the Lm unit response amplitude is also reported as an LC15-like neuron response (Fig 7-10).
data_and_independent_videos: Entirely synthetic stimuli rendered in MATLAB; no real video. Type 1 (Figs 2-6): random black/white dot texture field 180x90 deg, figure (34 deg square or 25 deg wide bar) moving over texture; variants Edge, Bar on Ground (bar and background opposite), Theta Figure, Theta Figure in Moving Background. Type 2 (Figs 7-10): imitation of Stadele et al. LC15 stimuli (small dark object, dark bar, wide-field grating, 180x70 deg). Type 3 (Fig 11): uniform grey 15 deg bar over 10 HDR natural still images (Meyer et al. HDR database) that are translated in the opposite direction at the same speed, 360x97 deg panorama. So the number of independent natural backgrounds is 10 still images; random-dot textures are procedurally generated (number of random texture instances per condition not stated [uncertain]). No train/test split exists because nothing is learned; parameters were hand-set, partly on the same stimuli used for evaluation (e.g. alpha raised for natural scenes).
target_size_and_input_resolution: Input resolution: 0.33 deg/pixel (types 1-2) and 0.39 deg/pixel (type 3) before a 12x12 Gaussian blur (sigma 3.5 px) and downsampling by factor 6, giving roughly 2 deg sampling per EMD unit (acceptance angle 2.7 deg / interommatidial 2.0 deg for types 1-2, 3.2/2.3 deg for type 3); the 180x90 deg field is therefore on the order of 90x45 EMD units [uncertain, derived not stated]. Target sizes: 34 deg square figure (~17 units), 25 deg wide bar (~12 units), 15 deg bar on natural scenes (~7 units), 8.9 deg bar in LC15 stimuli (~4 units); Fig 6A-B: 5 deg bars fail with large receptive fields, optimal Ir receptive field about 12x12 deg, default 14x14 deg (7 EMD units); Fig 2D: segmentation of the 34 deg figure needs Ir receptive field about 24x24 deg. Dot texture size 2.6 deg (and 7.9 deg in Fig 5B2).
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: EMD input updated every 10 ms (100 Hz); lobula units integrated with RK4 at 0.4 ms (25 sub-steps per frame). Speeds: mostly 66 deg/s (type 1), 33 deg/s (type 2), background -132 deg/s with varied bar speed in Fig 6C. Observer is stationary: no self-motion or camera motion is simulated; 'background motion' is a rigid translation of the background pattern (opposite to, or co-moving with, the figure), not optic flow from egomotion (no parallax, rotation, expansion or scale change).
detector_and_exemplar: No object detector and no exemplar: the target is not specified in any way; the figure emerges bottom-up wherever local motion differs from the surround in direction. Ground truth masks were manually annotated for evaluation only.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: None. Fully hand-designed feedforward network (no recurrence or feedback); parameters chosen manually: EMD time constants (tauHP 250 ms with 10% DC, tauLP 50 ms, ON/OFF rectification thresholds 0 and 0.05, noise threshold 0.002), Gaussian receptive field sizes of Ir/Il (default 7 EMD units), Im 3x3 kernel, 3x3 Prewitt-type lobula kernels, membrane tau 5 ms, reversal potentials (leak -50, exc 0, inh -80 mV), sigmoid theta -40 mV and beta 0.5, synaptic weight alpha_EMD->lo 150 (100 in Figs 7, 8, 11; ~300 boosts natural scenes), alpha_lo->lo 20 in methods but 2 in Fig 2 caption (internal inconsistency). Parameters are interpreted as candidates for adaptation/plasticity (octopamine-like theta shift), but no learning or loss is used.
controls_seeds_splits: Controls are stage-wise ablations and parameter sweeps, not matched learned baselines: F-measure compared at EMD output vs Ir/Il output (spatial smoothing) vs lobula output (spatiotemporal smoothing); sweeps of receptive field size (Fig 2D, 6A), membrane tau (Fig 5), bar width and dot size (Fig 6A-B), bar velocity relative to a -132 deg/s background (Fig 6C), contrast (Fig 6D), theta and beta (Figs 8-10), alpha (Fig 11); ON or OFF pathway blocking (slight F-measure drop); two-quadrant vs three-arm EMD robustness check. No random/shuffled network control, no comparison with computer-vision segmentation or background-subtraction baselines, no seeds reported (deterministic model; random texture realisations not counted [uncertain]). Fig 11 averages over 10 HDR scenes per speed with standard deviation. No data splits (no learning).
metrics_and_numbers: Metric: instantaneous F-measure (harmonic mean of pixel precision and recall of the thresholded binary mask vs manually annotated moving-bar ground truth; 0 = failure, 1 = perfect), threshold 50% of maximum response by default (Methods). Key numbers (text statements; exact curve values only in figures): Fig 2D - Ir segments the 34 deg figure once receptive field reaches ~24x24 deg. Fig 4 (B, D) - F-measure low at EMD output, raised to >0.8 at Ir output, robust over 10-90% thresholds; with moving background the best EMD-stage threshold shifts to ~70%. Fig 5A - segmentation fails for tau_m < 0.6 ms, robust from 0.8 ms; 5 ms sufficient for all stimuli; Fig 5B1 - Theta Figure in Moving Background needs tau_m ~1.6 ms, larger 7.9 deg dots (Fig 5B2) need longer. Fig 6A-B - optimal receptive field ~12x12 deg; 5 deg bars fail at large receptive fields; wider bars help with diminishing returns; dot size matters only at 2.6 deg. Fig 6C - background at -132 deg/s: works when bar moves opposite; 'Poor performance arose once the bar shared the same direction with its background' even at different speeds. Fig 6D - contrast >= 30% works well. Fig 7C - Lm depolarisation grows with bar height, insensitive to bar speed (LC15-like). Figs 8-9 - shifting theta from -40 to about [-28, -22] mV (Ir/Il) or [-30, -26] mV (with Im) restores LC15-like bar responses under background motion; Fig 10 - steeper beta alone does not rescue, beta plus theta shift does. Fig 11 - natural scenes: EMD output F-measure < 0.05; Il output improves over Il input, larger gain from spatiotemporal than spatial-only smoothing; raising alpha to ~300 boosts further, then saturates (exact Il values not given in text).
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: not applicable / no (no learning, no real videos; natural backgrounds are 10 still HDR images). Target absence: no (every stimulus contains a moving figure; no false-alarm rate on figure-free moving background reported). Similar distractors: no (single figure; no second similar moving object). Occlusion: no. Night or low light: no (authors state absolute illumination effects are out of scope; HDR scenes vary in lighting and RMS contrast 0.4-5.7 but no low-light test). Camera / self-motion: no (stationary observer; only rigid background translation). Same-direction figure and background motion: yes, tested and fails (Fig 6C). Sequential operation on own predictions: no (no tracking loop, no prediction feedback).
mechanism_summary: Published mechanism: (1) blur and downsample frames to a ~2 deg lattice; (2) signed two-quadrant ON/OFF correlation EMDs give local direction; (3) two direction-opponent interneuron maps Ir and Il pool the signed EMD map through wide Gaussian receptive fields (~12-14 deg) with opposite signs, i.e. each map is excited by one direction and inhibited by the other, implemented as conductance-based (shunting) leaky units with a sigmoid output threshold; a direction-neutral Im sums them; (4) lobula units Lr/Ll/Lm apply 3x3 edge-like (Prewitt) kernels to these maps; (5) membrane leaky integration (tau ~5 ms, at 100 Hz frame updates) provides temporal smoothing that the authors argue is key, together with spatial pooling, for turning noisy EMD output into a coherent figure mask. Figure-ground separation thus comes from direction opponency plus spatiotemporal smoothing plus a threshold nonlinearity, not from an explicit centre-minus-surround subtraction. Proposed (by authors, not tested as learning): octopamine-like shift of the sigmoid threshold theta, and higher synaptic gain alpha for natural scenes, as adaptive state modulation. Our earlier simplified version (one-gain surround subtraction on FlyVis output) did not reproduce: signed direction-opponent pathways (it subtracted a magnitude/mean surround), the shunting conductance nonlinearity with a tuned firing threshold, explicit temporal integration of the readout, the per-condition gain/threshold modulation, and edge-shaped lobula kernels; it also differed in that our target is approximately stationary inside a tracking crop while the background moves.
transfer_limits: 1) Temporal sampling: model runs at 100 Hz input with 5 ms membrane tau; our stand is 30 Hz, so per-frame displacements are ~3.3x larger and the EMD tauLP/tauHP correlation regime and the temporal smoothing benefit (Fig 5) are not validated; FlyVis integrates internally at its own dt but input changes every 33 ms. 2) Camera and crop motion: the paper uses a stationary observer with rigid background translation; our crop moves and rescales around the predicted track, so the target is roughly stationary in the crop and the background flows - a regime the paper never tests (closest is 'Edge' with stationary background, the reverse), and rescaling adds expansion/contraction flow that a direction-opponent L/R scheme does not model. 3) Same-direction failure (Fig 6C): when target and background move in the same direction in image coordinates (common under imperfect crop centering or when camera pans with traffic) the published network fails even at different speeds. 4) Scale: optimal receptive field ~12 deg vs targets 15-34 deg, i.e. figures of ~7-17 sampling units; our targets are ~9x12 hexal lattice steps on a 721-hexal grey lattice, comparable in units, but 5 deg (~2-3 unit) bars fail, so small/distant BDD100K objects are outside the working range. 5) Resolution and colour: grey input matches, but the hexal lattice is ~31 hexals across, so 12-14 deg pooling covers a large fraction of the crop and leaves little surround. 6) Task mismatch: the mechanism segments 'whatever moves differently'; it has no exemplar and cannot pick the previous target among similar neighbours moving with the same velocity, and has no refusal output; target absence and distractors were never tested. 7) Evidence regime: synthetic bars over 10 still HDR images, hand-tuned parameters (alpha raised for natural scenes), no real video, no low light; F-measure is not related to HOTA. 8) Environment: YOLO26s already supplies boxes; a figure mask only helps if it corrects the predicted centre during detector misses, which the paper does not address.
research_questions_addressed: Q1: caution - provides bottom-up figure-ground separation from relative motion, but no exemplar-conditioned selection among similar objects and no refusal; does not answer Q1 directly. Q2: design analogy - its stage-wise F-measure analysis (EMD output vs pooled vs temporally integrated readout) is a template for locating whether information is lost in the representation or in the readout; suggests our failure of surround subtraction may be a readout (opponency/temporal integration) issue rather than core representation. Q3: direct evidence of operating limits - works for opposite relative motion, contrast >= 30%, figures >~ receptive field scale, 100 Hz, stationary observer; fails for same-direction motion and tiny bars; nothing at 25-30 Hz or with moving camera, so it does not meet the Q3 answer-change condition. Q4: not addressed (no confidence or refusal). Q5: informs a cheap, parameter-light readout test (few hand-set parameters, no GPU training needed), and highlights that a control without FlyVis (EMD-only or raw-difference pipeline) is natural because the paper itself is FlyVis-free.
candidate_node_change: Node: readout (with temporal state) of FlyVis - replace the one-gain surround subtraction by a Wu-Guo-style direction-opponent, temporally integrated lobula readout on FlyVis T4/T5 outputs. Concretely: from stock FlyVis T4a-d/T5a-d activity form signed opponent maps per axis (e.g. right minus left, up minus down), pool each with a Gaussian of ~1/3 of the box size, pass through a conductance-style leaky unit (shunting excitation/inhibition, sigmoid threshold theta) integrated across the 30 Hz frames, and compute figure evidence as local opponent motion relative to the crop-frame background estimate (subtract the dominant crop motion first, since the target is near-stationary in the crop). Use the resulting map only as a centre-correction/refusal feature in the Z13 lost-track step. Controls: (B) the same opponent-pooling-integration readout computed on a FlyVis-free motion signal (frame-difference or classical Hassenstein-Reichardt/two-quadrant EMD on the same 721-hexal input, as in the paper) with identical parameters; (C) stock frozen FlyVis with the old one-gain surround subtraction; (D) the new readout on stock FlyVis. Minimal check: on the cached val7/train_cache dev crops with known target positions, measure useful-centre rate and mask/centre agreement (no HOTA first), with paired bootstrap over videos; parameters (pool size, theta, alpha, tau) fixed on train dev and frozen before test. Stop condition (write before running): if D does not exceed B by a paired-bootstrap interval excluding zero on useful centres, or does not exceed C, stop this readout (record node of failure: opponency vs temporal integration via ablation of each) and do not proceed to HOTA; also stop if performance collapses in the same-direction subset (target and background flow same sign in crop), which the paper predicts.
strongest_objection: The paper solves a different and easier problem: a single figure on a stationary observer's retina moving opposite to a rigidly translating synthetic or still-image background, at 100 Hz, evaluated by pixel F-measure with hand-tuned parameters (including a gain increase specifically for natural scenes). Our failure mode is identity selection among similar neighbours and refusal under a moving, rescaling crop at 30 Hz - exactly the conditions the paper never tests, and its own Fig 6C shows failure when target and background share direction. Moreover the mechanism needs no FlyVis at all (it is built on simple EMDs), so any gain from transplanting it risks being a readout/motion-segmentation improvement attributable to the external module rather than to FlyVis, which per the project boundary must be separated by the FlyVis-free control.
evidence_strength: Peer-reviewed (PLoS Computational Biology, 2023), open access; code publicly available (MATLAB, GPL-3.0; repository existence and file list verified, code not executed or line-checked). No independent replication found [uncertain]. Overall: weak for our decision - strong internal consistency as a computational-neuroscience model with systematic parameter sweeps, but synthetic stimuli, 10 still backgrounds, no real video, no moving camera, no learning or held-out evaluation, minor internal parameter inconsistency (alpha_lo->lo 20 vs 2), and no tracking-relevant metric.
